two_host_side_faults_of_mine_this_sessio.wedged_the_shell: I issued about 28 `menu` queries in one loop to find the recording format; the USB worker wedged with LIBUSB_ERROR_TIMEOUT moved=0/64 while the camera stayed enumerated. The skill warns against chaining many commands in one run. Recovery was a USB replug plus `pkill -9 -f fpshd` and one fresh daemon. Later runs sent a handful of commands with 0.8 s gaps and had no trouble.
two_host_side_faults_of_mine_this_sessio.wrong_inference_about_power: after the replug the cave was zero and the hook stock, and I concluded the camera runs on USB bus power so unplugging power-cycles it. The operator had cold-booted it themselves. Withdrawn.
two_host_side_faults_of_mine_this_sessio.an_earlier_recording_failure: before the wedge, a MOV pulse and an S2 pulse both left is_recording at 0 and wrote no clip. After the cold boot the same MOV pulse worked first time. The best available explanation is that the USB worker was already degrading and silently dropped the key events; not established, and not counted as a mode or card problem - the card had 74 GiB free.

a_one_off_not_explained: the first publish of the session reported 0xC000EABC (I-cache invalidate) as DID NOT RETURN, then five consecutive calls afterwards returned cleanly, as did every publish after the cold boot. It was the first invalidate of that boot, but it was also shortly before the wedge, so 'first of boot' is not established as the cause. The D-cache half succeeded and the arena had never been executed, so the placed image's visibility did not depend on it.
next_step_requires: a decision: arm bound-probe-two (one clip, non-destructive, seg never written) or release both blocks. Both blocks stay held until one or the other happens, or until a power cycle.
